description: ASELSAN MTAL'in teknik disiplinini güçlü bir dostlukla birleştiren BlockCode ekibiyiz. Adımız gibi her birimiz farklı bir renk ve yeteneğiz; bir araya geldigimizde kusursuz çalışan bir bütün oluyoruz. Masamızda sadece kod ve tasarım değil; kahkaha, çay molaları ve bitmeyen bir heyecan var. Tüm enerjimizi tek bir hedefe kilitledik: NASA Space Apps. Dostluğumuz ve üretme sevgimizle uzayın derinliğinize hazırız!
summary: Project Overview: The project is an interactive space mission design game built using block-based algorithms (Scratch). It features a 2D physics simulation, collision detection, and a dynamic difficulty system.   Gameplay & Mechanics: Players control a rocket's thrust using the spacebar to survive in orbit by avoiding obstacles made of accumulated space debris while increasing their score.   Objective & Social Responsibility: The main goal is to provide players of all ages—especially children—with a simple and entertaining experience while building early awareness about space pollution. Its social responsibility is to carry environmental consciousness beyond Earth to leave a clean space heritage for future generations.   User Experience: Designed with single-key playability, a fluid game loop where obstacle speeds adapt dynamically, and a clutter-free interface for quick, accurate reactions.   Vision & Mission: Its vision is to make space exploration free from complexity through technology and design, creating a learning environment where curious individuals can understand, experience, and generate new ideas. Its mission is to simplify complex space data through Scratch gamification so that everyone can learn science through hands-on experience.
details:
Space Mission Design Game is an interactive 2D simulation built on Scratch for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Players control a rocket's thrust using a single key—the spacebar—to navigate through Low Earth Orbit (LEO) while avoiding dynamically adapting obstacles made of accumulated space debris.

Vision & Mission: Our vision is to remove complexity from space exploration through technology and design, creating an accessible learning environment. Our mission is to gamify complex space data on Scratch so people of all ages—especially children—can learn science through hands-on experience while raising early awareness about space pollution and environmental responsibility beyond Earth.

NASA Data & Tech Stack: We integrated real-world NASA datasets to ensure scientific accuracy. Obstacle frequency and dynamic difficulty progression are scaled using Low Earth Orbit debris density data from the NASA Orbital Debris Program Office, while flight physics (fall acceleration and ascent speed) are modeled on Earth’s actual gravity and NASA Launch Telemetry. Built with Scratch's block-based algorithms, the project also utilized generative AI tools (Gemini, Claude, and ChatGPT) to simplify datasets, debug code, and generate visual and textual assets.
